cues.text: Good morning, what can I do for you?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Uh, yes, I am currently visiting this area, but I injured myself when I was doing sports a while ago, and I still feel painful, so I wondered whether I could go for a doctor here.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Sure sir, we can take you on as a temporary patient. I'll just take down some personal details of you. May I have your name, please?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Yes, it's Peter Smith.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: All right, Peter. And where are you currently staying here?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: At 95 Cross Street
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: And the county?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Walkley. That's W-a-l-k-l-e-y.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: OK, and can I have a contact number?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: OK, thanks. May you just wait down there! The doctor will see you in a minute.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Now, how can I help you? It's Peter Smith, isn't it?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Yes, I had a sporting accident, and a doctor at home treated me, but I'm still getting some pain.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Hum, right. Uh, first of all, I want to ask you a few questions.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Okay.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Well, what sport were you doing when you got injured?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Playing tennis with my friends.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Now, I see. Did you hurt your elbow or wrist?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Oh, no. I had my knee sprained, which was the original problem.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Right, and when did this happen?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Uh, that was three weeks ago now, so it was about June 18th.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Hum. And, you said you had medical treatment at home?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Uh, yeah. The doctor said I didn't need an X-ray or things alike, and he just told me to use an ice pack.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Fine, anything else?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Yes, and I've been using a walking stick to help me get around.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Right, now what problems are you having during walking?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Well, actually I can walk, yet I still can't go upstairs, so I've been sleeping downstairs.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Hum, now you said your knee still gets hurt?
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Well, no. Actually, it's getting better. It's my back that's hurting, me now. It really aches at night, and I cannot sleep well.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Hum, I have several suggestions for that.
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Great.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: First you should put the stick away as that's probably the source of the problem.
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Oh, really? I wish I'd know.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: After that, I can prescribe you something to relax the muscles in your back
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Oh, sorry to be difficult, but I've had something like that in the past, and there were many side effects, and I don't want to take it. Would you recommend anything else?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Well, yes. We do have a leaflet showing some exercises you can do yourself at home. If you do them every day, they'll soon be effective.
cues.speaker: Doctor

cues.text: Great. I'll do that.
cues.speaker: Peter
